evidence: records/evidence/discovery-coverage-linux-20261111-evidence.tar.gz (SHA-256 27edfaf32595aca6562ab0ff7a58f16f470d52c68f3b8f23fec9f33c167a5368): probe and measurement scripts with the exact fixture and configset, phase logs, every saved request/response with headers (setup, placement, combined and individual facets filtered and unfiltered, both facet-comparison tables, Luke passes with and without distrib=false and fq, segment state, failure and tolerant responses, timeAllowed attempts with full bodies, measurement grid and environment samples, cluster status snapshots, teardown listings), plus the first attempt's responses under runs/attempt1.
head: 82888694ae248b74d105d9c7b5f60d33c385f325

legs.environment: Linux htch-runtime (kernel 7.0.0-44), 4 CPUs, 7.9 GB RAM, Temurin JDK 21.0.12.1, packaged Solr 11.0.0-SNAPSHOT built by :solr:packaging:installDist at head 82888694ae248b74d105d9c7b5f60d33c385f325 in a clean clone. Two packaged nodes (ports 18983/18984, second node joined the first node's embedded ZooKeeper), IPv4 stack forced for the server JVMs. The first installDist attempt failed at :solr:webapp:verifyUiWasm because the egress relay corrupted the solr-ui-wasm.zip download (checksum mismatch); the zip was seeded from nightlies.apache.org at the pinned sha256 654494303e4af3b8bfb26a83d250603f19033820295591d88db0597991ce8ad2 and the build then passed. Environment only; no branch code involved.
legs.facets: rows=0 JSON query facets (one existence query per field) under filter cat_s:infilter and unfiltered, distributed and per shard (distrib=false on the hosting core), compared against expectations enumerated from the fixture manifest plus verified placement (a nested child matches the filter only on its own fields). Filtered: 28 of 30 field cells match exactly, including the domain totals; unfiltered: 28 of 30. Matches cover: multivalued field counted once per doc (d1 contributes 1 despite two values); dynamic field present on one shard only (1 on shard1, 0 on shard2, 1 distributed); field present only outside the filter (0 under the filter, counted unfiltered); deleted-only field ghost_s (0 everywhere after deletion); DocValues-only field dvonly_s (counted 1 via doc values); never-present field (0). The only mismatches, in both scopes and both filters wherever the field is present (distributed and shard1): storedonly_s returns HTTP 400, IllegalStateException: FieldExistsQuery requires that the field indexes doc values, norms or vectors, but field 'storedonly_s' exists and indexes neither of these data structures. Where the field is absent (shard2) the same query returns 0. A combined request carrying all ten fields in one facet block fails wholesale with the same 400 on the distributed and shard1 paths. Nested domains: under the plain parent-field filter the child is a separate domain (childkind_s counts 0 filtered, 1 unfiltered); parent and child are therefore not interchangeable coverage domains. Classification: existence facets are a sound coverage mechanism for indexed and DocValues fields; a stored-only field is not 'absent', it is unsupported and actively breaks the request.
legs.failure: With the node hosting shard1 stopped (connection refused verified): the default distributed facet query and a default select both return HTTP 503 with no results. With shards.tolerant=true both return HTTP 200 with partialResults=true in the response header and surviving-shard-only data (facet domain count 2, select numFound 3, exactly shard2's live docs); the facet response in tolerant mode includes buckets for fields the surviving shard can answer. The node was restarted afterwards; cluster status captured immediately after the restart still showed the replica state down (recovery lag), and it returned to active service for the later passes.
legs.fixture: Collection disccov, 2 shards, RF=1, configset uploaded unchanged from the head's _default conf, three fields added through the Schema API (idxonly_s indexed-only, dvonly_s DocValues-only, storedonly_s stored-only). Routing is controlled by composite-id prefixes resolved empirically and verified per shard: prefix r1 to shard1, r0 to shard2. Verified placement: shard1 holds d1 (multivalued multi_ss with two values, dynonly_s dynamic field, all three special fields), d2, d3 (outside_s, outside the filter), the parent p1 with nested child p1-c1, and the ghost doc before deletion; shard2 holds d5, d6, d7. The ghost doc was indexed and hard-committed, then deleted by id with a hard commit and no merge; its segment retains delCount=1 (segments evidence in the archive). Disclosed correction: the first setup attempt put _route_ in the document body, which the compositeId router ignores (placement was id-hash order); that collection was deleted and the fixture was rebuilt with id-prefix routing, which is the run all results below come from. The first attempt's raw responses are archived under runs/attempt1.
legs.limit_partial: A deterministic partial result was produced with timeAllowed=1 on the distributed facet request: with shards.tolerant=true, all five attempts return HTTP 200 with partialResults=true and partialResultsDetails naming TimeAllowedLimit (Limits exceeded ... Query limits: [TimeAllowedLimit:LIMIT EXCEEDED]). Without tolerance, all five attempts return HTTP 503. Caveat recorded: the cluster status captured just before these attempts still showed shard1's replica as down after its restart, so the non-tolerant 503s may mix the limit with replica recovery; the tolerant partial is attributed to the limit by its own response details. Classification: completed via the timeAllowed limit; facet counts in the partial responses are the pre-limit partial aggregates and are not treated as coverage data.
legs.luke: numTerms=0 captured distributed, per core, and in fq pairs, in two passes. Pass 1 (no distrib=false): every response, from either core and from the collection path, is byte-equivalent in content: the same 13 field names (including ghost_s, dynonly_s, storedonly_s, childkind_s) and the same mixed index stats (numDocs 8, maxDoc 6, deletedDocs 1); fq never changes the result. That pass is collection-aggregated enumeration, not per-shard truth. Pass 2 (distrib=false on each hosting core): shard1 lists 13 fields with index numDocs 5, maxDoc 6, deletedDocs 1; ghost_s is still enumerated with docs=1, so a deleted-only field remains visible in local segment metadata until a merge removes it. shard2 lists exactly its own 8 fields; ghost_s, dynonly_s, storedonly_s, dvonly_s, childkind_s are absent. Per-field docs counts in local Luke are inverted-index counts: idxonly_s reads 1, dynonly_s 1, but dvonly_s reads 0 and storedonly_s reads 0 even though a live doc on shard1 carries both (the facet leg counts dvonly_s as 1 through doc values). Internal fields _root_ and _version_ appear in every enumeration. Classification: local Luke enumerates field names present in a shard's segments (including deleted-only fields) and ignores fq; it cannot by itself distinguish live coverage, because its counts miss DocValues-only and stored-only presence entirely.
legs.measurements: Bounded grid on synthetic collections discmeas1 (1 shard) and discmeas2 (2 shards), 120 docs each carrying 50 m*_s fields, filters matching 100 and 20 docs, explicit facet field counts 1/10/50, 2 warmup plus 3 measured requests per cell, client wall-clock latency. All 12 cells returned the correct domain counts. Single-shard latency 0.0033 to 0.0080 s per request across all cells (field count has no visible effect at this scale); two-shard latency 0.0127 to 0.0869 s with wide variance on loopback. Process CPU sampled from /proc/<pid>/stat (utime+stime) around the whole grid: node1 +137 ticks, node2 +61 ticks; peak RSS (VmHWM) about 811 MB and 767 MB, dominated by the JVM baseline. Method and raw samples are in the evidence (measurements-env.txt). Descriptive only; data sizes are tiny and these numbers are not a resource bound. Unmeasured, by design of this round: cells above 50 fields, matching sets above 100 docs, and any concurrency above 1.
legs.teardown: All probe nodes stopped through bin/solr stop; final process listings after both the measurement/failure phase and the Luke pass show zero remaining Solr processes. The disc-cov clone is at the exact head with a clean git status. No production source was modified anywhere; probe scripts, fixture, and the uploaded configset copy live only in the evidence archive.

summary: Research feasibility round 1 completed at the exact head with every leg run and classified. Explicit-list JSON query facets over a known filter reproduce independently enumerated live-doc existence counts for indexed, multivalued, dynamic, DocValues-only, and deleted-only fields, in distributed and per-shard scopes, with one systematic exception: a stored-only field that is present in the domain makes the existence query fail with HTTP 400 (FieldExistsQuery requires doc values, norms, or vectors), and it poisons a combined multi-field facet request the same way; where the field is absent the count is 0. Luke enumeration without distrib=false is collection-aggregated (same 13 names and mixed stats from every core) and does not change with fq; with distrib=false it is per-shard accurate for field names, including a deleted-only field, but its per-field doc counts are inverted-index counts (DocValues-only and stored-only fields read 0). A downed shard gives 503 by default and 200 with partialResults=true and surviving-shard-only results under shards.tolerant=true. timeAllowed=1 produces a deterministic partial result whose response details name TimeAllowedLimit. No production code was changed; nothing was pushed or posted.
